سُتْرَةٌ : see سِتْرٌ. ―
-b2- Its predominant application is to A thing which a person praying sets up before him; [sticking it in the ground, or laying it down if the ground be hard, in order that no living being or image may be the object next before him;] such as a whip, and a staff having a pointed iron at its lower extremity. (Mgh.) [See عَنَزَةٌ: and see my “ Modern Egyptians, ” 5th ed., p. 72.] ―
-b3- Also A parapet, or surrounding wall, of a flat house-top. (Mgh.) ―
-b4- And i. q. ظُلَّةٌ [q. v.]. (Mgh.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
